findings.title: One project's non-UTF-8 git output freezes the whole local board indefinitely: UnicodeDecodeError is not in GIT_ERRORS, so it escapes the per-project failure boundary the spec built for exactly this

evidence.value: local/tabs.py:104-109 -- try: if is_repo(run, root): built[pid]['git'] = git_tab(root, stamp, run) / except GIT_ERRORS as e: warn and carry

local/tabs.py:49 and :56 call run(...) with text=True, encoding='utf-8', i.e. strict decoding. git log --pretty=format:%h|%ad|%s is run with no limit over the whole history (local/tabs.py:68), so a single commit subject written under a non-UTF-8 i18n.commitEncoding -- or a non-UTF-8 branch name from branch --show-current -- makes subprocess.run raise UnicodeDecodeError, which is neither an OSError nor a subprocess.SubprocessError.

With the injected run raising a real UnicodeDecodeError for alpha's git log call only: the exception escapes tabs.build, run_pass raises, db.upsert and db.delete are called zero times, and a full id,doc snapshot of every record table read from a SECOND connection is byte-identical before and after -- the healthy second project, the sessions, runs, projects, catalogue and meta/lastRefresh all lost for that pass. The contrast case (the same exception class raised one call earlier, from a document read) is confined and carried as the spec requires.

collector._one catches it, prints 'pass failed (UnicodeDecodeError: ...); nothing written', returns 1, and the interval loop goes straight to the next pass (local/collector.py:685-696) -- so the condition repeats every 60 seconds indefinitely while the local board stays frozen at its last good state.

findings.impact: Spec 4.2.1 row 3 rules that a TimeoutExpired or OSError from any git call costs that project's git tab alone, and the whole rationale of 4.2.1 (round-1 finding F-6) is that a per-project source fault must never destroy every record of every pass, every 60 seconds, indefinitely. A git call whose output is not valid UTF-8 is a per-project source fault of exactly that class, and it is the one git failure the handler does not catch. It is mitigated relative to a silent freeze -- the board's own export_board.main catches UnicodeDecodeError as the ValueError subclass it is and exits 2, so refresh.py pushes nothing either, and the local failure is loud on stderr once per pass -- which is why this is MEDIUM and not HIGH. But the local consequence is strictly worse than the board's: the board's failure is one watched tick, the collector's is a permanently stale local app.
findings.remediation: Add UnicodeDecodeError to tabs.GIT_ERRORS and update the adjacent comment, which already states the author's intent as any git failure. There is no row-2 versus row-4 collision to reintroduce, because the load_data carve-out is already scoped outside this block. Add one case to local/tests/test_tabs.py PerProjectFailures alongside the existing TimeoutExpired case: a run that raises UnicodeDecodeError for one git call leaves the git tab unbuilt with a warning, the stored one carried, and the pass committing. Decoding the git subprocesses with errors='replace' would also work but diverges from export_board's decoding, so it should be a spec question rather than a code choice.

findings.title: An every-scenario guard on the statuses table was deleted rather than re-expressed, so no PBI-019 scenario now checks which status records a pass writes -- and the change report calls it 'none removed'

evidence.value: for table in ('project_tabs', 'statuses'): self.assertEqual(c.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM %s' % table).fetchone()[0], 0, table)

change-report.json line 65 states of the three edits: 'Each is re-expressed to the new behaviour; none is weakened or removed'. Two of the three (the kinds set at test_collector.py:812 and the summary regex at :869) are genuine re-expressions; this one is a removal with no replacement.

Only test_collector.Records.test_only_the_kinds_the_collector_writes_are_written still observes statuses in that suite, and only for one fixture. The Status class in local/tests/test_tabs.py covers the rule itself well (8 cases), so the loss is breadth in the PBI-019 suite, not the rule.

findings.impact: The tearDown ran after every PBI-019 collector scenario. Its statuses half was the only broad check that a pass writes no status record it should not. Its removal is not wrong, since the collector now writes statuses by design, but it trades an invariant for nothing, and the deviation is reported as though no assertion was dropped, which is the part a reviewer would otherwise have to rediscover.
findings.remediation: Re-express rather than delete: assert in tearDown that the ids in statuses are exactly the statusDoc paths of the projects the scenario configured (an empty set for the many scenarios that configure none), which keeps the every-scenario invariant and still passes under the new behaviour. Separately, correct the change report's wording for this one edit to 'two re-expressed, one removed', so the disclosure matches the diff.

follow_ups.ref: spec pbi-025-local-tabs.md section 4.4 row 4 -- plan defect, fix the spec not the code
follow_ups.reason: Row 4 reads: the tab was not built, a record is stored, and it already has carriedSince -> Store nothing. Taken literally that omits the record from the intended set, which puts it in the deletion set and deletes it on the third carrying pass. I verified this by replacing tabs.carry with the literal reading: test_tabs.Carry.test_the_full_carry_cycle fails. The code's choice (return the stored document unchanged so it stays intended, and let the unchanged-ignoring-generatedAt check in _Pass.store suppress the write) satisfies both halves -- db.upsert calls for the tab kind counted at zero on pass 3 -- and is the only reading consistent with section 6.2. The builder disclosed this; the right disposition is a one-sentence spec amendment to row 4, not a code change.

Recommend annotating section 7 as satisfied-by-merge so it is not read as a live constraint by the next PBI in this cluster.
